title: Rangers Move Cal Quantrill to Injured List Amid Growing MLB Trade Rumors Surge
body:
The Texas Rangers placed right‑hander Cal Quantrill on the 15‑day injured list Thursday afternoon after doctors diagnosed a strain in his right latissimus dorsi. The move shuffles the bullpen that has been a key factor in the club’s surge to the top of the American League West, and it triggers the recall of right‑handed reliever Winston Santos from Triple‑A Round Rock.

Quantrick, 28, entered the season as a middle‑relief specialist and quickly evolved into one of the team’s most dependable swing‑men. Over his 23 appearances before the injury, he logged 21⅔ innings, posting a 2.90 ERA, striking out 28 batters and limiting opponents to a .210 batting average. His ability to bridge the gap between starter and closer has allowed Texas manager Bruce Bochy to preserve his high‑leverage arms for later innings, a strategy that has paid dividends as the Rangers have compiled a 73‑49 record and sit five games ahead of the Seattle Mariners.

The lat strain, which appears to be a Grade 1 tear, is expected to keep Quantrick sidelined for at least two weeks, though the team’s medical staff will reassess his status after the standard 10‑day rest period. In the meantime, the Rangers have turned to Winston Santos, a 24‑year‑old right‑hander who spent most of the season in the minors after a brief major‑league stint in 2022. Santos brings a fastball that can sit in the mid‑90s and a developing slider, and he will be tasked with filling Quantrick’s role as a left‑handed‑hitter neutralizer in the middle of the game. The club’s front office indicated that Santos’ promotion is “a direct response to the immediate need for a reliable right‑handed option” and that they expect him to be a short‑term solution while they explore longer‑term depth options.

The Rangers’ bullpen, already featuring stalwarts such as Nathan Eovaldi, Brock Burke and closer Jose Leclerc, has been a cornerstone of the team’s success this season. Quantrick’s absence does not dramatically alter the overall makeup, but it does thin the pool of middle‑relief arms that can handle high‑leverage situations against left‑handed batters. In recent weeks, Texas has relied heavily on Eovaldi in a hybrid starter‑reliever role, and Burke has been called upon more frequently to eat innings. The added workload could test their durability as the season pushes deeper into the stretch run.

Analysts note that the Rangers’ front office has been proactive in bolstering bullpen depth throughout the campaign, acquiring veterans like Burke at the trade deadline and signing free‑agent relievers to short‑term deals. The injury to Quantrick underscores the importance of that strategy and may accelerate discussions about additional moves before the July 31 deadline. Potential targets could include a left‑handed specialist to balance the right‑handed heavy lineup or a versatile swing‑man who can handle both high‑leverage and long‑relief duties.

Looking ahead, Texas will need to maintain its bullpen stability as the AL West tightens and the postseason race intensifies. If Winston Santos can adapt quickly to the big‑league environment, he could provide a bridge until Quantrick returns. Otherwise, the Rangers may have to dip deeper into their farm system or explore the trade market to keep the pressure on rivals. The next few weeks will be a litmus test for the club’s depth and its ability to navigate injuries without sacrificing the momentum that has carried it to the summit of the division.
